records.title: 6T70/6T75 Transmission Wave Plate Failure
records.description: First-generation Enclaves (2008-2017) use the 6T70/6T75 6-speed automatic, whose stamped-steel 35R wave plate can crack at the teeth after enough shift cycles. When it fractures, the transmission abruptly loses 3rd, 5th, and reverse gears, and debris can damage the valve body, drums, and torque converter. Failure typically occurs in higher-mileage 2008-2012 builds.
records.solution: Disassemble and rebuild the transmission with an updated/stronger wave plate, plus replace damaged hard parts and clean out debris; in severe cases a remanufactured unit is installed.
symptoms: Sudden loss of 3rd, 5th and reverse gears

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption / Engine Failure on 3.6L
records.description: Higher-mileage first-generation Enclaves with the 3.6L V6 (worst on the 2008-2010 cars) can burn oil excessively, and in the most severe cases the engine fails outright, including reports of a hole punched in the block. The condition is linked to the same engine's timing-chain/oiling weaknesses and is addressed in GM's diagnostic guidance (PIP5084). Owners who don't monitor oil level risk progressive engine damage.
records.solution: Diagnose per GM PIP5084; remedies range from PCV/oil-control updates to, in severe consumption or block-failure cases, engine replacement (around $6,500). Check oil frequently between changes as a stopgap.
symptoms: Frequent need to add oil between changes
Knocking or engine failure in severe cases

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure
records.description: Enclaves commonly suffer failed HVAC blend-door actuators, with the plastic internal gears stripping or the small motor dying, often after about 80,000 miles. Because multiple actuators control temperature blend, vent direction, and recirculation, a failure leaves one zone stuck hot or cold, or produces a clicking/knocking sound behind the dash. The part itself is inexpensive but labor varies widely by which actuator failed.
records.solution: Replace the failed blend-door actuator and recalibrate the HVAC system. Some actuators are easy to reach; others require significant dash disassembly, which drives up labor.
symptoms: Clicking or knocking noise behind the dash
One side blows hot while the other blows cold

records.title: Loss of Power Steering Assist (Pump Wear)
records.description: 2008-2011 Enclaves (and platform-mates Acadia/Traverse/Outlook) can develop a power steering pump wear condition that causes an intermittent drop in hydraulic pressure and sudden reduced or lost steering assist. The vehicle reverts to manual steering requiring much greater effort, most noticeable at low speeds and during parking. GM issued a Special Coverage Adjustment covering the condition for 10 years/150,000 miles rather than a formal NHTSA recall.
records.solution: Replace the power steering pump (and inspect/replace fluid and lines). Covered under GM Special Coverage for 10yr/150k mi on affected vehicles; otherwise replace the pump out of pocket.
symptoms: Steering suddenly becomes hard to turn
Heavy steering at low speed / parking

records.title: Enclave Power Steering Assist Loss — Special Coverage Adjustment 14329
records.description: GM Special Coverage Adjustment 14329 — extending warranty to 10 years / 150,000 miles — covers 2008-2011 Buick Enclave, 2007-2011 GMC Acadia, 2009-2011 Chevrolet Traverse, and 2007-2010 Saturn Outlook for power-steering pump wear that causes intermittent drop in hydraulic pressure and loss of steering assist. This is a special coverage program, NOT a recall — owners must initiate the claim. Symptoms: heavy steering at low speed, especially when engine is hot.
records.solution: Confirm Special Coverage 14329 eligibility at any GM/Buick dealer with your VIN. If still within 10 years and 150,000 miles, remedy is free: dealer flushes power-steering system, replaces the PS pump, and installs a new steering-gear valve housing. If out of the coverage window, expect $700-$1,400 for the same job at an independent.

records.title: Rear A/C Evaporator Corrosion & Refrigerant Leaks
records.description: Many 2013-2016 Enclaves lose air conditioning because fine copper particles ejected from the rear blower motor settle on the rear evaporator and, combined with condensation, corrode it and cause pinhole refrigerant leaks. High-pressure A/C lines can also leak at connections from vibration and corrosion. Owners notice the system gradually stops blowing cold, with no obvious external cause.
records.solution: Recover the refrigerant, replace the corroded rear evaporator (and rear blower motor if shedding debris) or the leaking line, then evacuate and recharge the system. Confirm leak source with dye/UV before recharging.
symptoms: A/C blows warm or only intermittently cold
Oily residue near A/C line connections

records.title: Stretched/Worn Timing Chain on 3.6L V6
records.description: The 3.6L (and 2.8L) high-feature V6 in 2008-2013 Enclaves is prone to timing chain stretch and worn chain guides/tensioners, sometimes appearing as early as 40,000-60,000 miles. As the chain elongates, valve timing drifts, triggering misfires and a rattle at idle/startup; if a chain jumps a tooth it can bend valves and cause catastrophic engine damage. GM acknowledged the defect (occurring even with regular oil changes) and issued Special Coverage Adjustment #11340C extending the chain warranty to 10 years/120,000 miles on affected engines.
records.solution: Replace the timing chains, guides, and tensioners (a full front-of-engine job). If covered under GM Special Coverage #11340C the repair is free up to 10yr/120k mi; otherwise it is an out-of-pocket repair. Keeping oil changes current and using correct-spec oil slows wear.
symptoms: Rattling noise at idle or cold startup

records.title: Enclave 3.6L LLT Timing Chain Stretch + Oil Consumption
records.description: Early Enclaves (2008-2012, plus shared Traverse/Acadia/Outlook) with the 3.6L LLT direct-injection V6 share LaCrosse's timing chain stretch and a separate excessive-oil-consumption issue. The PCV system pulls oil into the intake, intake valves carbon up (no port injection to wash them), and the chain wears prematurely from stretched OLM intervals.
records.solution: Timing chain replacement ($2,500-$4,500 with 3-row crossover labor premium). Walnut-blast intake valve carbon at the same time ($300-$500). PCV system update per TSB. Some owners refuse the chain job at this mileage and trade — failure can mean total engine replacement ($6,000+).

records.title: Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Shudder
records.description: Both the 6-speed (first-gen) and the 9-speed 9T65 (second-gen, 2018+) Enclaves are prone to a torque converter clutch shudder felt as a vibration or 'chuggle' during light acceleration, low-speed lockup, or while climbing grades. On 2018-2019 models GM traced many cases to incorrect transmission fluid installed at the factory, addressing it under TSB 18-NA-091 (and PIP5608C). Left unaddressed, the shudder can accelerate clutch and converter wear.
records.solution: Per GM bulletin: flush and refill with the specified DEXRON-VI fluid (part 88862156) and reprogram the TCM with a fast-learn relearn. Persistent cases may require torque converter replacement.
symptoms: Chuggle or jerk when transmission locks up

records.title: Water Pump Leak / Coolant Loss on 3.6L V6
records.description: The 3.6L V6 in the Enclave is known for water pump failure, attributed in part to dissimilar metals in the pump that expand and contract at different rates and eventually allow coolant to seep. Owners frequently find coolant puddling after the car is parked and may see overheating if the leak is severe. It is considered a fairly routine wear item on this engine.
records.solution: Replace the water pump (and thermostat/gasket as needed), then refill and bleed the cooling system. A relatively common, moderate-cost repair on these vehicles.
symptoms: Coolant puddle under vehicle after parking
